findings.source: apps/web/src/shared/ui/Header.tsx:59 clearTimeout(timeoutId) before Header.tsx:68 await res.json()
findings.claim: The 4s gateway deadline is cancelled when headers arrive, so a JSON body that stalls is never aborted. Because only the latest check may write, a run of stalled bodies leaves the last label (for example a healthy RTT) in place for as long as the stall lasts; in production this is bounded only by upstream/proxy timeouts (nginx /healthz location sets no proxy_read_timeout, default 60s).
findings.counterexample: H3: first check JSON ok -> 'Gateway: 0ms' (fake clock); every later response has JSON headers and a body that never resolves until aborted. After 60s and 13 checks the label is still 'Gateway: 0ms'.
findings.minimalFix: Keep the timer until after res.json() (clear only in finally) so the abort also rejects the body read and maps to Offline/degraded. Verified in scratch (FIX3): H3 passes, author H1/H2 and the rest unchanged.

info: UI-R2-I1 Design differs from Root's literal M1 wording (skip a background tick while the same resource is in flight, release only the owning request in finally). The author instead issues every tick and applies any completion newer than the last applied one. Behaviour meets the closure targets in the probes: no starvation (R3), bounded concurrency (2 for 6s responses, 3 for hangs, given a 10s timer and 5s interval), older completions never overwrite newer applied data (P4), no shared in-flight guard that an old scope could release.

UI-R2-I2 Only the latest controller per resource is kept in xAbortRef. On unmount, logout and project switch, older overlapping requests are not aborted. They end via their own 10s timer (R7) and are dropped by the session/scope/applied fences. No data leak; transport cancellation is not complete.

UI-R2-I3 The approve/reject guard is real (R8 0 decide calls; R8c control: the same click path with approvals current calls decideApproval once). handleReject rethrows into ApprovalDetail's try/finally without a catch, which leaves one unhandled promise rejection per blocked click (R8 unhandled=1). This predates R2.

UI-R2-I4 '비정상 응답' covers both contract errors (HTML 200, JSON 404) and a reachable unhealthy endpoint (503, status!=ok), with no HTTP status shown. This is acceptable under the L1 minimal fix; a status suffix would help operators.
UI-R2-I5 fetchX(isBackground: boolean | any) widens the type to any. Strict === true makes it safe at run time; boolean plus a separate manual callback would keep tsc protection.
UI-R2-I6 Timeout copy hardcodes '(10s Timeout)'. Under UI-R2-L1 that text also appears for user cancels.
